architectureComparison.intro: Archipelago and FactoryBench share the central idea that an agent should act through tools in an isolated world and be graded from observable outcomes. FactoryBench adds a released Oracle-shaped schema, task-level control checks, exact answer fields, and full public oracle replays.

rows.left: Containerized task environments with snapshot lifecycle
rows.right: Per-task SQLite snapshots generated from public synthetic seed records
Three MCP namespaces: oracle_erp, plant_docs, factory_harness
Harness records every read, transaction, rejection, and submission
State assertions + read order + exact answer + write scope + errors
GitHub world, Hugging Face rows, Harbor tasks, and website explorer

architectureComparison.title: The same evaluation spine, assembled for manufacturing ERP

benchmark.name: FactoryBench-100
benchmark.question: Can an agent run the factory workflow—not just describe the next screen?
benchmark.tagline: 100 executable manufacturing ERP workflows over an Oracle-shaped factory world.

leaderboard.name: gpt-5.6-luna
leaderboard.note: Fixed 10-task stratified sample: one released task from each workflow family (10/100); not full-suite coverage.

leaderboard.name: Reference oracle
leaderboard.note: Measured solvability ceiling from replaying the checked-in reference workflow; not a model submission.

leaderboard.name: Incomplete-workflow control
leaderboard.note: Measured ablation that omits the final ERP mutation while still submitting the oracle answer.

leaderboard.name: Read-only control
leaderboard.note: Measured control that performs the required reads but makes no ERP changes or answer submission.

leaderboard.name: No-control ablation
leaderboard.note: Measured ablation that skips all policy and preflight reads; the environment rejects its writes.

methodology.body: FactoryScore is the mean percentage of deterministic checks passed. Each task checks required reads before writes, exact ERP state transitions, exact answer fields, write-scope containment, and tool-call validity. Strict completion is shown as supporting evidence, not a second benchmark metric.
methodology.title: One metric, inspectable evidence

methodology.body: The suite is a clean-room simulation shaped by real manufacturing operations: multi-record order intake, SKU and supplier preflight, approval limits, transactional rollback, lot-level inventory, tax-and-amount reconciliation, and production recovery. It contains no Oracle binaries, proprietary screens, customer records, or copied benchmark tasks.
methodology.title: Real workflow shape, synthetic company data

methodology.body: The release replays every reference workflow, replays a deterministic sample twice, runs three negative controls, and removes every reference mutation one at a time. Qualification passed: 100/100 reference strict passes; 240/240 mutation omissions were detected; impaired controls remain below the oracle.
methodology.title: Qualification before publication

methodology.body: Enterprise-Bench informed noisy multi-system task framing; ERP-Bench informed long-horizon manufacturing coverage; Mercor APEX informed the public task, asset, environment, and trajectory presentation. FactoryBench tasks, records, tools, and verifiers are independently authored and executable under this repository's licenses.
